lines.trans: Denis, can I ask you to take this up to the luxury suite?
Can you not go yourself? Well, Kostik does not allow me to go into guest rooms.
What if there is an undressed man in there?
Come on, please.
Maybe they will even give you a tip.
Whoa! A tip?
Let me take it up. Yeah right, so you can gobble up half the basket on the way.
No thanks.
Denis, please.
Fine. Which room?
Luxury suite 311.
Is it really that hard to remember which suite is occupied and which is free?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask (a favour)', paired with 'просить'.

examples.trans: I wanted to ask you something.
Arkash, I wanted to ask you something.

meanings.en: to carry, deliver something to a place
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to carry / take up', paired with 'относить'.

examples.text: Я сам отнесу блюдо в зал.
examples.trans: I will carry the dish into the dining room myself.
Take the documents to the boss.

examples.text: Я сейчас сам отнесу в зал.
examples.trans: I will carry it to the hall myself right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'luxury suite' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть люкс.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always luxury suite.
The chef immediately noticed where the luxury suite was.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'myself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'решать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'allows'.

examples.text: Ты мне костюм, а я разрешаю опоздать.
examples.trans: You get me the suit, and I allow you to be late.

examples.text: Сегодня тебе разрешат играть со всеми игрушками.
examples.trans: Today they will let you play with all toys.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number; phone number; hotel room' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Don't laugh. Read me the number.

meanings.en: to walk, to go on foot
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go (regularly)'.

examples.text: Мальчик ходит на костылях. А она ещё и активистка.
examples.trans: The boy walks on crutches. And she's an activist, too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'suddenly, what if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'man' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У мужчины бывает не только жена.
examples.trans: A man can have more than just a wife.
This man is waiting for you.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'одетый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('undressed').

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень неодетый выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very undressed choice.

examples.text: У нас сегодня просто неодетый день в ресторане.
examples.trans: We are having a simply undressed day at the restaurant today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common neuter noun meaning 'tips' in everyday Russian.
Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'they will give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'according to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рога'). Common feminine noun meaning 'road' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какая разница, кто будет строить дороги?
examples.trans: What does it matter who builds the roads?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лкорзины'). Common masculine noun meaning 'half the basket' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть полкорзины.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always half the basket.
The chef immediately noticed where the half the basket was.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лопать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'gobbled up'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и слопать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and gobbled up on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют слопать.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to gobbled up.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('what').

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'three hundred', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А для него это как триста!
examples.trans: And for him it's like three hundred!
The ticket costs three hundred roubles.

examples.text: Триста пятьдесят миллионов рублей по смете!
examples.trans: Three hundred and fifty million rubles per estimate!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'eleventh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно одиннадцатый и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite eleventh and calmly.

examples.text: На кухне всегда одиннадцатый кипит работа.
examples.trans: Work is always bustling eleventh in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'ужели').

examples.text: Неужели так трудно найти хороший сюжет?
examples.trans: Is it really so difficult to find a good story?

examples.text: Неужели президент накажет вас за правду?
examples.trans: Will the president really punish you for the truth?
Do you really not care at all?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'льзя').

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'помнить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remember / memorize', paired with 'запоминать'.

examples.text: Вот так на митингах говори, запомни.
examples.trans: That's how you talk at rallies, remember that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('busy').

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вободный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('free (to go)').

examples.trans: That's all, Samson, you can go!
